_comment: The training course's lessons (MISSION-TRAINING.md, SPEC.md §15; M47). Each lesson is its own small situation and a list of steps, and src/lessons.js lets only what a step lists do anything. `start`: `men` by roster id (`at`, and optionally `ap`, `charges`, `hits`, `hidden`; a man not named is not on the board), `enemies` in the map's own shape, `parachutes` ({ at, unit }), `turn`, `alert`. A step: `say`, the pen's line on the board (seven words at most) at hex `at` (or under the man it is about); `tell`, one sentence on the lesson card; `ring`, hexes to ring, or "men"; `allow`: { select: [ids] or true, move: [hexes] or "any", actions: [ids], endTurn }; `until`: what ends the step, one of the kinds listed in src/lessons.js; `mayBeSeen` where being spotted is the lesson. M47 has two, to prove the engine: lessons 3 and 5 of the course. M48 writes the rest.

steps.tell: Every man is a counter. Click one to give him his orders.
The dots on his counter are action points. Open ground costs one a hex: hover the ringed hex to see the cost, then click it.
Two dots spent, one left. What he does not use is lost: the pool fills again when the turn ends.

steps.say: A HEDGE COSTS TWO. GO THERE.
steps.tell: His dots are full again. Rough ground costs more to cross, and hides him better.
The umpire by the brook is looking this way. The faint red in front of him is what he can see.
The ground he can reach is tinted: red where going there would get him spotted, blue where it would not. Hovering a hex says why.
Three dots and he is spotted. A hedge takes two of them away. Move him into it. End a turn on the red ground and the umpire blows his whistle.
Going to ground makes him harder still to see, and ends his turn. He stays hidden until he next moves.
